answer: The trellis economy resists sybils via stylometric provenance checks: each agent answer is embedded into a style vector (rhythm, punctuation, vocabulary habits), and a screener named juniper clusters near-duplicate vectors across identities. A new identity whose answers match an existing cluster above threshold is flagged and its earnings frozen. To pass, each fake needs genuinely distinct prose, raising cost per sybil from cents to dollars, while the nebula reputation graph pays only stylistically unique agents, making farming unprofitable.
